subject: VPC licensing & platform fee — commercial alignment and implementation credit
messages:
From: Alice Chen <procurement@omnicare.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: David Lin <cto@omnicare.com>, contracts@omnicare.com
Date: Fri, 05 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood private deployment pricing questions

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for the demo last week. We have a few commercial questions that are blocking our procurement review, specifically around the VPC/on‑prem licensing model and the platform fee amortization. High level:

- We plan to run Redwood in our VPC across two regions; we expect ~250ms median latency for inference and 3M generated tokens/mo.
- Procurement needs clarity on whether the platform fee is capitalized or treated as an OPEX line item (accounting asks).
- We would like to understand the available implementation credit framework (you mentioned migration credits) and how that trades off against commit length.
- Support tiers: we want to confirm SRE on‑call coverage vs. premium support pricing and whether we can tier support by environment (prod vs. non‑prod).

Can you share a short term sheet and a couple of pricing options that show: (A) 24‑month commit + 1x implementation credit, (B) 36‑month commit + 2x implementation credit, and (C) a metered consumption option with a smaller platform fee?

We'd like to close procurement gating items by next week.

Thanks,
Alice Chen
Head of Procurement
OmniCare Health


From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Alice Chen <procurement@omnicare.com>
Cc: David Lin <cto@omnicare.com>, contracts@omnicare.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood private deployment pricing questions

Hi Alice —

Appreciate the clear list. I'm attaching a short commercial term sheet and an initial pricing matrix that lays out the three structures you asked for (RDW-OMC-term-sheet-v1.pdf). Quick summary up front:

- Platform fee: can be amortized over 6, 12, or 24 months for procurement purposes; we typically recommend 12 months for mid-sized deployments to align with operational ramp.
- Implementation credit: offer ranges from $50k (12‑month) up to $200k (36‑month) depending on commit and scope — see sheet.
- Support tiers: Standard, Enhanced (SRE retainer + 24/7 escalation), and Premium (SRE + named oncall + quarterly runbooks). Environment scoping (prod vs non‑prod) is supported — non‑prod can be on Standard while prod is on Enhanced.

I looped in Marissa (account lead) to surface a few flexible pricing levers that might fit OmniCare's procurement needs. If you can confirm which commit horizon you prefer, we can draft a signature‑ready term sheet and route to Legal/Finance.

Attachments: RDW-OMC-term-sheet-v1.pdf (term summary)

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555‑0198

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, Alice Chen <procurement@omnicare.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 06 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood private deployment pricing questions — pricing options attached

Hi Alice / Jonas —

Attaching a workbook with three pricing scenarios and a short ROI sheet (RDW-pricing-options-omnicare.xlsx). A few pragmatic notes from a commercial perspective:

- Implementation credit: we can structure as a one‑time invoice credit applied to the first 3 invoices, or as a prepayment reduction of the platform fee. For accounting flexibility we recommend the invoice credit approach (simpler for your AP team).
- Platform fee amortization: we can publish an invoice schedule that shows the platform fee amortized monthly over a chosen horizon; legally the fee is a subscription but we provide schedule for capitalization.
- Commit sensitivity: if OmniCare can commit to a 24‑month minimum and a baseline committed spend of $1.2M ARR, we can offer a $120k implementation credit + 15% off Enhanced support for prod environments.
- Alternatively, a 36‑month commit at $1.5M ARR buys $210k credit + free onboarding hours (up to 300 ops hours) and Premium support pricing locked for the term.

Open items for your procurement: billing entity (corp vs regional), PO cadence, and whether you want the non‑prod nodes counted toward commits (we usually exclude non‑prod but can include them at a discounted rate).

If helpful we can run a short cost‑comparative deck with your finance folks next week.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Alice Chen <procurement@omnicare.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: David Lin <cto@omnicare.com>, contracts@omnicare.com
Date: Sat, 06 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood private deployment pricing questions — our priorities

Thanks Jonas / Marissa —

Quick response from procurement and engineering after reviewing the term sheet:

- Procurement prefers the invoice credit approach you mentioned.
- Our finance team will treat the platform fee as CAPEX if we can get a 12‑month amortization schedule and a signed SOW demonstrating the implementation scope.
- Engineering prioritizes having Premium support for first 6 months of rollout, then downgrading to Enhanced. That is non‑negotiable for go‑live risk.

To be actionable, we need: (1) a call with Redwood legal to confirm contract language about platform fee treatment, (2) a redline‑friendly term sheet that reflects a 24‑month commit with $150k implementation credit, and (3) confirmation the Premium support for months 0–6 is included in the credit structure or billed separately.

I've attached our SOW draft (OmniCare_SOW_vA.docx) to show expected scope. Can we aim to have a redline by Tuesday?

Best,
Alice Chen
Head of Procurement
OmniCare Health

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Alice Chen <procurement@omnicare.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, legal@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood private deployment pricing questions — proposed commercial response

Alice / team —

Thanks for the quick read‑through and the SOW. Proposal below that addresses your three asks and keeps the path to signature tight: 

1) Implementation credit: We can offer a $150,000 implementation credit conditioned on a 24‑month committed spend (baseline $1.2M ARR). Credit structure: applied as invoice credits across the first four monthly invoices (can be compressed to first two if you prefer).

2) Platform fee amortization: Redwood will provide a monthly amortization schedule (12 months by default) for accounting. Legal note: the underlying commercial instrument remains a subscription/license fee; the schedule is for your finance reporting. We'll loop Legal to confirm language that states "invoice schedule provided for customer accounting purposes".

3) Premium support: We will include Premium support for months 0–6 bundled into the implementation credit (no additional invoice for months 0–6). After month 6, support will move to Enhanced for prod as discussed and Standard for non‑prod.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa to push a redline term sheet (I will update RDW-OMC-term-sheet-v2 with these points).
- Legal sync: I can schedule a 30‑minute call with Redwood Legal + OmniCare Contracts on Tuesday 09/08 at 10:00 AM PT — does that work?
- DocuSign link will be generated once redlines are accepted; HubSpot deal updated with updated MRR/ARR numbers.

If that frame works, we'll get the redline out this afternoon and confirm the legal call.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
